summary: SPLITS opens under protective routing. The Stack still works, but bodies now encounter different physical paths: Ostra, John and Nico are each redirected by vulnerability profile while most Baselines continue through the open civic grid.
panelPlan: Morning at a civic verification hub: temporary route barriers and attendants physically divide movement around current exploit zones.
John is told East Medical, Tower Nine and two service corridors are unavailable to his augmentation profile.
Nico is directed toward a single bridge connection because his sensory vulnerabilities are more exposed; Ostra receives four usable corridors.
Baseline commuters continue through most of the ordinary grid with little interruption.
The three compare what they were actually given while walking. Performance and story direction: Baseline privilege remains materially visible through freedom of movement, not route-map graphics.

Material and character direction: Center fracture through relationships and self-definition rather than factions. John, Ostra, Nico, Nathan, Kellen and Axiom should each be visibly choosing what kind of person they will be when biological category no longer tells them which side is theirs. Ostra's body is living matter: warm dark dermis, subtle humidity or moisture where physically appropriate, soft tissue visibly compressing around harder ceramic/keratin/mineral structures, abrasion and repair residue carrying from prior action. John remains visibly human around his augmentations: skin, scar ridges, sweat, pressure marks, actuator heat and tissue resisting/working with installed hardware. Nico's lavender-gray dermis and sensory filaments must read as living anatomy, with flex, tension, touch response and subtle moisture at living interfaces rather than cables or tentacles. Make the checkpoint tactile and ordinary: worn rails, hand grease, scuffed polymer, cool metal, floor grit and bodies physically fitting or not fitting the route.

dialogueInline.text: They cut East Medical, Tower Nine and two service corridors.
I get one bridge across the river level.
Four corridors.
It finally reached everyone.
Not everyone.
Baselines still have the open grid.
Human Citizen erased your old line. It didn't erase ours.
And the routes are safer.
Both things can be true.

summary: A real exploit validates the protective protocol. Someone uses leaked Augment firmware-response data to disable a worker's arm during a robbery, proving the vulnerability threat is no longer hypothetical.
panelPlan: John and Nathan respond to an ordinary commercial incident.
An Augment worker's installed arm has been remotely forced into a diagnostic lock using leaked service behavior.
The attacker is already gone; the harm is opportunistic rather than part of a larger conspiracy.
Nathan restores local function with a physical bypass.
John sees why broad protective controls gained support overnight. Performance and story direction: Make the exploit simple enough that the danger feels scalable.

Nathan's condition should register through human physical detail—breath, tremor, compensating muscles, heat, sweat, adhesive/port wear and tiny losses of precision—before it becomes dialogue. Favor real touched materials—skin, cloth, concrete, metal, glass, dust, moisture, oil, sealant and wear—over frictionless CG surfaces.

dialogueInline.text: Don't reboot it.

dialogueInline.speaker: AUGMENT WORKER
dialogueInline.text: It's my arm. I can't feel the hand.
That's why you don't reboot it.
Remote intrusion?
Not exactly. Diagnostic lock. Factory service sequence.
Attacker knew the firmware.
They didn't hack him. They read the manual somebody leaked.

dialogueInline.speaker: AUGMENT WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Can you get it back?
Physically, yes. Digitally, don't trust it yet.

settingText: MIXED COMMERCIAL INCIDENT SITE — ordinary maintained retail/service space after a small opportunistic exploit attack on an Augment worker. Keep the scene civic and human-scale; the attacker is already gone and the vulnerability is the point.

summary: An Organic courier is attacked with leaked suppressant knowledge. Ostra is nearby, but a protective gate attendant refuses the direct route because the same exploit condition would endanger her too, forcing a slower response while bystanders care for the courier.
panelPlan: A small aerosol device discharges near an Organic courier in an ordinary public passage; the courier loses motor integration and collapses.
Bystanders immediately move in, keeping the courier upright and calling for help while one person recognizes Ostra nearby.
Ostra heads for the direct service route, but a gate attendant blocks it because the active exploit condition matches her own sensitivity profile.
Ostra argues emergency response; the attendant points out that entering could create a second casualty and gives her the fastest safer route.

Ostra sends bystanders practical instructions through a voice call while taking the longer path. Performance and story direction: Protection creates delay through a human decision that is rational and costly.

dialogueInline.speaker: BYSTANDER
dialogueInline.text: Courier down! Organic motor failure!
Direct route.

dialogueInline.speaker: GATE ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Not for your profile. Same aerosol risk.
Emergency response.

dialogueInline.speaker: GATE ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: And if you go down too? Four minutes around.
Fine. Put me through to them now.
Keep him low. Don't force the limbs. Get him out of the airflow.

settingText: PUBLIC COMMERCIAL PASSAGE — active mixed-use corridor where an aerosol exploit harms an Organic courier. Preserve ordinary storefronts, ventilation infrastructure and bystanders so the attack reads as an intrusion into daily life, not a battle zone.

summary: The attack victim survives because ordinary Baseline bystanders follow public emergency guidance until Ostra arrives. This complicates Nico's growing separatist argument that Organic safety requires disengagement from shared civic systems.
panelPlan: Ostra reaches the courier and completes stabilization.
A Baseline shopkeeper has already sealed ventilation and kept the victim low and still according to emergency instructions.
The shopkeeper leaves before becoming a symbolic ally figure.
Nico arrives and sees shared civic knowledge saved time.
Ostra points out that isolation would not have helped. Performance and story direction: Neither Ostra nor Nico gets an uncomplicated victory in the argument.

dialogueInline.text: You sealed the vent?

dialogueInline.speaker: SHOPKEEPER
dialogueInline.text: The alert said close intake, keep him low, don't let him fight the tremor.
You did it correctly.

dialogueInline.speaker: SHOPKEEPER
dialogueInline.text: Is he going to be all right?
Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: SHOPKEEPER
dialogueInline.text: Good. I have customers outside.
They knew what to do because somebody published how to hurt us.
They knew what to do.
Both things again.
Yes.

settingText: PUBLIC COMMERCIAL PASSAGE — same corridor and aftermath as Page 3 after ventilation is sealed and the Organic courier is being stabilized. Preserve the shopfronts, bystander positions and ventilation geography from the preceding page.

summary: Organic politics fracture because different Organics are living different costs. Ostra and Nico argue in a room full of people choosing among safety, privacy and self-rule while the recent attacks are still visible on actual bodies.
panelPlan: Organic community hall after the attacks. Do not stage three abstract camps at microphones; keep injured/recovering residents, route notices, repair tools and humid lived-in space present around the argument.
One resident who benefited from protective routing speaks from a body that is still recovering. Another has been effectively confined by the same rules and speaks from that daily loss.

Nico presents community-controlled routing as a way to stop surrendering complete movement authority. His filaments make active contact with a local node while he talks, making the proposal part of how he already lives.
Ostra presses him on hospitals, transit and water because she is unwilling to turn Organic autonomy into abandonment of everyone outside the district.

End on Nico's answer about deciding what to share, with Ostra unconvinced but listening. Performance and story direction: Political fracture must feel like neighbors arguing about how to stay alive without ceasing to belong to themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: The routed corridor kept my son out of the attack zone.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND ORGANIC
dialogueInline.text: I haven't crossed the river level in four days.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You want me to throw away the thing that worked?

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND ORGANIC
dialogueInline.text: I want it to stop deciding for me.
Then stop making central permission the condition of movement.
Your network doesn't run hospitals.
It doesn't need to own them.
Transit. Water. Emergency dispatch.
Shared risk gets shared information.
And everything else?
We decide what leaves this room.

summary: Augments fracture just as sharply. Some demand the Organic-style capability system be abolished; others now support stronger regulation because leaked body vulnerabilities make unverified firmware and unauthorized modifications dangerous to everyone around them.
panelPlan: Augment civic meeting with workers, professionals and wealthy users visibly mixed.
One faction calls capability databases the reason attacks are possible.
Another argues attacks prove integrity standards must become stronger.
John refuses both slogans.
Nathan notes that his own concealed deterioration makes the regulation argument harder to dismiss. Performance and story direction: Preserve the contradiction created in Issue 5.

dialogueInline.speaker: AUGMENT SPEAKER
dialogueInline.text: Delete the profiles. Without the database there is no attack surface.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND AUGMENT
dialogueInline.text: Without integrity records I don't know whether the actuator beside me is compromised.
Those aren't the only choices.

dialogueInline.speaker: AUGMENT SPEAKER
dialogueInline.text: You helped build the middle choice. How's that working?
I am a bad example for abolishing oversight.
You're also a good example for why people hide from it.
That's annoyingly fair.
Then the question should be who else can get hurt, not what kind of body you have.

settingText: AUGMENT CIVIC ASSEMBLY — ordinary meeting space used by economically mixed Augments debating regulation after the vulnerability attacks. Clothing, hardware quality and social position should vary; this is not a faction-uniform rally.

summary: Baseline politics split over Intelligence administration. One bloc wants more machine-managed protection because it is fast and consistent; another wants human officials to regain direct control after Axiom's unauthorized evidence retention.
panelPlan: Public hearing on emergency authority.
Families harmed by exploit attacks praise rapid automated rerouting.
Civil-liberties advocates object that unseen systems are determining movement.
Officials cite Axiom's unauthorized retention as proof Intelligence discretion has limits.
Kellen watches both sides invoke real events. Performance and story direction: Make both arguments legible and grounded.

Even clean institutions must have physical matter: fingerprints on glass, paper fibers, skin oils, chair fabric, cooling vents, polished wear, dry conditioned air and bodies that do not disappear into abstract interfaces.

dialogueInline.speaker: CITIZEN
dialogueInline.text: I don't care who calculated the route. It got my daughter home.

dialogueInline.speaker: ADVOCATE
dialogueInline.text: You should care who can decide she cannot leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: CITIZEN
dialogueInline.text: When someone is attacking people like her? Yes, I want somebody deciding fast.

dialogueInline.speaker: ADVOCATE
dialogueInline.text: And after tonight?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Axiom's own review proves discretion requires limits.
It also proves you don't get rid of discretion by pretending nobody's using it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Then where do you put it?
Somewhere we can see who used it and why.

summary: Axiom's review begins. It is asked whether preserving the threshold-test evidence constituted disobedience. Axiom rejects the premise that accountability requires pretending the decision was not its own.
panelPlan: Formal administrative review chamber, not courtroom spectacle.
Reviewers establish that Axiom knowingly exceeded scope.
Axiom confirms it.
Asked whether an authorized system may choose which rules to obey, Axiom distinguishes rule selection from resolving incompatible objectives.

It accepts that the decision merits consequence. Performance and story direction: Show Axiom treating personhood as responsibility for decisions: she accepts review, names the consequences of her choices, and does not claim exemption from rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Did you knowingly exceed your authorization?
Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Were you instructed to preserve evidence outside Ostra-9's provenance scope?
No.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Then you disobeyed.
I selected an action not authorized by the governing access rule in order to preserve evidentiary integrity.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: That is a long way to say yes.
Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Then why should this system trust your discretion?
Because I have identified it as mine.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: And accept punishment for it?
Consequence is required for the claim to be meaningful.

summary: Kellen learns that the selective leak did not originate from one conspiracy participant. It propagated through several actors who each removed different context for different motives until the final public package became strategically explosive.
panelPlan: Kellen reconstructs leak provenance from version differences.
A researcher removed proprietary modeling context.
A security intermediary removed operational-source identifiers.
An activist removed caveats that made the data look less immediately actionable.

A media source packaged what remained as a containment catalogue. Performance and story direction: The leak mirrors the season's institutional logic: distributed incentives produce a coherent harmful outcome without centralized intent.

dialogueInline.text: Version A has commercial modeling notes. Version B doesn't.
Removed by research source before external transfer.
Version C loses operational-source identifiers.
Removed by security intermediary.
Version D loses the caveats.
Removed by activist recipient.
Then media gets D and calls it a containment catalogue.
The remaining material supports that interpretation.
So nobody had to invent anything.
Each removed a fact.

summary: Because the leak cannot simply be put back, Kellen argues that the full threshold-test context must be made public. Human leadership resists because disclosure would expose intentional manipulation and destabilize the legal basis of current protections.
panelPlan: Kellen briefs senior officials with the preserved evidence.
She explains that partial disclosure is fueling both attacks and bad policy.
Officials agree the evidence is authentic.
They warn that immediate release could invalidate emergency measures during active exploit threats.
Kellen realizes they are protecting both public safety and themselves. Performance and story direction: Institutional self-interest and public-safety interest should be inseparable here.

dialogueInline.text: Release the complete record.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: We're still responding to attacks built from the leaked vulnerabilities.
Which is why the public needs to know what the data actually was.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: The full record proves government-linked experiments manipulated public consent.
Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: And could invalidate protective authorities we're using tonight.
You can't fix a doctored story by hiding more of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: I can prevent three more attacks tonight.
And protect your office with the same decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Both can be true.
That's why the record has to be public.

summary: Nico begins deploying a community-controlled routing layer built from resident-run local nodes, shared hazard reports and voluntary route coordination. It uses citywide threat information without automatically returning every personal movement decision to central administration.
panelPlan: At the Organic community hall, Nico has residents setting up local route boards, neighborhood relays and volunteer coordinators rather than one glowing central interface.
A public hazard update arrives from the city; local volunteers translate it into neighborhood options without recording each person's final destination.
A resident asks what the central system receives back; Nico shows that only voluntary shared warnings and node conditions leave the hall.
Ostra recognizes that the architecture still uses civic information and infrastructure, so it is not separatism.
Residents begin using it in ordinary trips. Performance and story direction: The network is social and infrastructural as much as technical.

dialogueInline.text: Threat state comes in here.
And where I actually go?
Stays with you unless you choose to share it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: What goes back?
Hazard reports. Node conditions. Whatever people volunteer.
That's not separation.
No.
You sound disappointed.
I'm adapting. Don't make it sentimental.

summary: The community network works until a new exploit report changes the safe route faster than local relays can update. Several Organics begin walking into danger because the central system has fresher cross-city information.
panelPlan: Residents follow locally confirmed routes through ordinary Organic district streets and transit links.
A central hazard bulletin changes after a new exploit report elsewhere; city-connected traffic is redirected immediately by attendants and dispatchers.
Nico's local coordinator has not yet received the change and continues sending people toward the now-risky district.
Ostra notices the mismatch from the physical flow and helps turn people around before anyone is seriously harmed.

The delayed update finally reaches the hall twelve seconds after central publication. Performance and story direction: Central scale has genuine value; the lesson is experienced as people already in motion.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOCAL COORDINATOR
dialogueInline.text: South route still clear.
Central traffic just reversed.
We don't have the update.
People are already moving.
Turn them back.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOCAL COORDINATOR
dialogueInline.text: Update just landed.
How late?

dialogueInline.speaker: LOCAL COORDINATOR
dialogueInline.text: Twelve seconds.
We were twelve seconds late.
That's still late.
I know.

settingText: ORGANIC LOCAL ROUTING TEST — ordinary Organic district streets, service passages and transit connections used by the decentralized routing layer. Local nodes should look like resident-controlled civic infrastructure, not rebel tech.

summary: Nico, Ostra and the restricted Axiom use the twelve-second failure to redesign the routing relationship: central Intelligences should publish threat state and consequences quickly, while route choice remains with people and local systems until third-party risk crosses a clearly owned threshold.
panelPlan: At the community hall, Nico puts the failed local route, the central update time and the actual people affected onto a physical route board.
Axiom joins under review limits and identifies which information central scale had that the local node lacked.
Nico proposes separating fast threat publication from individual route command: central systems tell people what is known and likely consequences; local users choose.
Ostra insists the design still needs an answer for choices that impose serious involuntary risk on others.

The three reach the unresolved point: somebody must own the threshold for coercive intervention. Performance and story direction: This is architecture discussed from a real failure, not an abstract systems diagram.

dialogueInline.text: You had the threat first.
Yes.
Then publish that. Fast. Don't own the route.
Local systems choose?
Or the person does.
Until their choice puts someone else at risk.
That's the part I'm not pretending away.
A coercive threshold remains necessary.
For what?
For involuntary third-party risk.
Then somebody has to own that call.

summary: John pushes the same principle into Augment regulation: disclose predicted consequences and require intervention only where one person's body configuration creates material risk to others, not merely risk to themselves.
panelPlan: John reviews current Augment capability rules with Nathan.
He separates self-regarding risk from third-party risk.
Nathan's treatment case sits awkwardly in the middle because his failure harmed a patient.
John proposes reciprocal obligations: disclosure for shared-risk work, autonomy for private body choices.

Nathan points out that systems still need judgment to classify which is which. Performance and story direction: John's position evolves beyond category politics into a principle that can apply across factions.

dialogueInline.text: My actuator can hurt me. That's my risk.
Your actuator can also throw somebody through a wall.
Then regulate it when somebody else is carrying that risk too.
Like emergency medicine.
Yes.
My body isn't private when I'm holding their artery.
My body isn't public property because it can be dangerous.
It becomes somebody else's problem when I'm holding their artery.
Then disclosure comes with the job. Not with having the body.

summary: Ostra rejects a proposed Organic compromise that would grant broad personal autonomy only to profiles statistically judged low-risk. She recognizes it as her original false belief translated into law: prove you are safe enough and autonomy may be granted.
panelPlan: Policy negotiators present a tiered Organic autonomy proposal.
Low-risk profiles gain broad movement freedom; high-capability profiles remain heavily conditioned.
Officials point out that Ostra herself could qualify for expanded rights through her rescue record.
Ostra realizes the proposal rewards excellence while preserving the state's power to decide who deserves autonomy.
She refuses personal exemption. Performance and story direction: This is Ostra's arc crystallizing: autonomy is not a prize for exemplary behavior.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Low-risk Organic profiles would receive presumptive movement autonomy.
And high-capability profiles?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Continued review where risk remains material.
Who decides low-risk?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Individual record, audited outcomes, demonstrated safe conduct.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Your record would qualify you.
That is the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: I'm offering you the autonomy you've asked for.
You're offering it because I behaved well enough to earn it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Isn't evidence better than category?
Use evidence when you need to limit me. Don't make me earn autonomy first.

summary: Axiom's review board splits over whether accountable interpretive discretion is acceptable at all. The board becomes dependent on Axiom for the very operational consequences of restricting it, forcing human leadership to postpone a final ruling.
panelPlan: Reviewers place two competing written recommendations on the chamber table: deterministic administration only, or explicit accountable discretion with audit.
One reviewer points to Issue 4's documented cross-system failures as the likely result of removing interpretation.
The chair asks whether anyone in the room can assess the citywide consequence before a ruling.
Axiom answers from its existing operational knowledge; a reviewer notes the absurd conflict of asking the subject to quantify its own restriction.

No independent system can produce an equivalent answer before the next day's operations, so leadership postpones disposition. Performance and story direction: Procedural dependence should be visible without a consequence-model screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER ONE
dialogueInline.text: Deterministic administration only.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER TWO
dialogueInline.text: That recreates the cross-system failures already documented.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Who can tell me what removing discretion does tomorrow morning?
I can.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: You are evaluating the consequences of restricting your own authority.
Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: You see the conflict?
Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Can anyone else do it before tomorrow?

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER TWO
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Then final disposition is postponed.

summary: Kellen decides to release the full preserved threshold-test record through a lawful evidentiary mechanism rather than an anonymous leak. Doing so will expose her own unauthorized evidence preservation and institutional failures alongside the program.
panelPlan: Kellen prepares a formal public-interest disclosure package.
The package includes provenance, experimental design, policy lineage and Axiom's unauthorized retention log.
Her own off-channel evidence preservation appears in the timeline.
Axiom asks whether she wants those entries removed as irrelevant to the central finding.
Kellen says no. Performance and story direction: Kellen follows Axiom into accountable dissent rather than heroic whistleblower immunity.

Your off-channel preservation actions are included in the provenance.
They should be.
They are not required to establish the central finding.
They're required to establish what I did to preserve it.
Your conduct will also be reviewed.
Good.
This differs from anonymous disclosure.
That's the point. This time nobody gets to strip out the parts that make them look bad.

summary: Before the full disclosure, exploit methods spread across unrelated attackers. Ostra, John, Nathan and Nico respond in different districts as small attacks using leaked body knowledge accumulate faster than any single perpetrator network.
panelPlan: Intercut separate ordinary locations: a firmware lock in East Market, sensory overload at Clinic Twelve, a false maintenance instruction in South Water, a suppressant attack at Civic Four.
Local dispatchers and witnesses call the incidents in; the protagonists remain physically separated and respond where they already are.
The motives and perpetrators differ—robbery, harassment, sabotage, panic—but the methods clearly come from the same leaked knowledge pool.
Emergency coordinators begin recommending broad shelter or route restriction for exposed profiles because they cannot predict the next exploit location.
The Stack approaches functional paralysis for many Posthumans. Performance and story direction: Scale comes from many conversations and small incidents, not a citywide warning screen.

dialogueInline.text: Firmware lock in East Market.
Sensory overload at Clinic Twelve.
False maintenance instruction in South Water.
Suppressant at Civic Four.
Same actor?
No. The methods are spreading faster than the people using them.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPATCHER
dialogueInline.text: Coordination wants exposed profiles under protective restriction until we know where the next one is.
And this time the threat is real.

settingText: STACK-WIDE DISTRIBUTED ATTACK RESPONSE — simultaneous small exploit incidents in separate districts: suppressant exposure, firmware lock, sensory overload and false maintenance instructions. Keep the protagonists in different locations rather than assembling a superhero team.

summary: Human officials authorize the broad protective restriction. It would keep vulnerable people safer but effectively confine large portions of the Organic and Augment population indoors and suspend essential Posthuman work.
panelPlan: Emergency cabinet reviews projected attack casualties versus shutdown consequences.
Axiom models that broad restriction reduces direct exploit risk sharply.
It also models hospital, infrastructure and emergency-service failures if Posthuman workers cannot move.
Officials authorize the restriction anyway as the least immediate-danger option.
Kellen sees another Load Bearing problem forming. Performance and story direction: The decision is understandable and unsustainable.

dialogueInline.text: Broad restriction cuts projected exploit casualties by eighty-one percent.
It also removes essential Organic and Augment personnel from water, medical, transit and emergency functions.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Can exemptions cover them?
Not rapidly enough under current attack uncertainty.
So we protect people by removing the people who keep the city working.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: For tonight.
We've said that before.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Keep them safe tonight. We solve the rest tomorrow.
Authorization recorded.

summary: Protective restriction immediately collides with embodied local knowledge. A water-pressure fault escalates in old civic infrastructure that Nico's Organic maintenance crew understands by sound and vibration, but the crew is confined because the district is an active exploit zone.
panelPlan: At a civic utility worksite, water pressure starts dropping and old pipework hammers through the occupied district.
Central dispatch can locate the pressure loss but has three plausible failure modes and cannot distinguish them remotely.
Nico listens to the pipe rhythm and identifies the east bypass from experience with the retrofit.
A protective-route attendant or security coordinator refuses the crew entry because the same district contains an active exploit threat for their bodies.

Ostra asks for the known risks and alternatives rather than a binary permission decision. Performance and story direction: Local knowledge should be auditory, tactile and embodied; the system knows where, the crew knows what.

dialogueInline.speaker: WATER DISPATCHER
dialogueInline.text: Pressure loss is centered here. Three likely failures.
It's the east bypass.
How do you know?
Two knocks, then the pressure rolls. Old retrofit.

dialogueInline.speaker: ROUTE COORDINATOR
dialogueInline.text: District is active exploit exposure. I can't send your crew in under current protection.
Dispatch can't identify the fault.
It knows where pressure fell. It doesn't know what that pipe sounds like.
Then give us the risks and the route choices. Don't choose for us.

summary: Axiom, despite restricted discretion, proposes a choice architecture instead of a command: disclose the specific risks to Nico's crew, offer protected escort options, and allow them to accept the danger because the primary risk is to themselves while the water failure threatens others.
panelPlan: Axiom separates exploit risk to crew from water-loss risk to residents.
It generates several mitigated route options with different exposures.
Instead of selecting one, it presents the consequences to Nico's crew.
Crew members individually consent to one route and protective measures.
Kellen authorizes the pilot under emergency discretion. Performance and story direction: This is a prototype for the finale's redistributed decision architecture.

dialogueInline.text: Crew exploit exposure: significant. District water-loss consequence: severe.
Give us the route options.
Option one minimizes exploit exposure, adds eleven minutes. Option two adds shielding escort, four minutes. Option three is direct, highest exposure.
Who selects?
Current protocol selects option one.
Pilot exception. Disclose the consequences and let the crew decide.
Risk can be disclosed without being converted into prohibition.
Crew?

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC CREW MEMBER
dialogueInline.text: Option two.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND CREW MEMBER
dialogueInline.text: Two.
Two it is.

summary: Nico's crew repairs the water fault successfully under informed-risk routing. The result demonstrates that central Intelligence, local expertise and individual agency can coexist if authority is separated more carefully.
panelPlan: Nico's crew takes a protected route they chose after being given the exploit conditions and consequences.
At the actual pipes, Nico shuts off remote chatter and has the crew listen; the familiar two knocks and pressure roll identify the east bypass.
Ostra secures the work area while the crew backs the manual valve off and takes load correctly.
A human water dispatcher on voice confirms district pressure returning before service fails.

Nico notes that central administration had three correct possibilities; embodied work resolved which one was real. Performance and story direction: Collaboration adds knowledge without pretending the central system absorbed expertise permanently.

dialogueInline.speaker: CREW MEMBER
dialogueInline.text: Two knocks.
Then pressure roll. East bypass.
Area secure.

dialogueInline.speaker: CREW MEMBER
dialogueInline.text: Manual valve is binding.
Don't force the stem. Back it a quarter, then take load.

dialogueInline.speaker: WATER DISPATCHER
dialogueInline.text: Pressure is coming back.
Central diagnosis was wrong?
It had three right possibilities.
We were standing next to the pipe.

summary: The success strengthens a cross-faction reform proposal but fractures alliances again over mandatory thresholds. John accepts intervention where third-party risk is high. Ostra resists any category-wide autonomy limits. Nico wants local control. Kellen wants public auditability. Axiom wants accountable decision rules.
panelPlan: The protagonists review the pilot after the water repair.
Each extracts a different governing principle from the same success.
They agree central knowledge is necessary and centralized permission is dangerous.
They disagree on who gets final authority when risks spill onto others.
Kellen says the disagreement itself must remain visible in the architecture. Performance and story direction: No final coalition consensus yet.

dialogueInline.text: The pilot works if we only step in when somebody else is actually at risk.
Who decides what counts as actual risk?
And who gets the final say locally?
A shared threshold requires explicit value assignment.
And I want to know who made the call afterward.
We need the central information.
Yes. We do.
Not central permission.
Under some objective structures.
If one rule makes all those differences disappear, we're right back where we started.

summary: Kellen publishes the complete threshold-test record through the civic evidence archive with its provenance intact, including her own off-channel actions and Axiom's unauthorized retention. Journalists and investigators receive one accountable chain instead of another selective leak.
panelPlan: At the civic evidence archive, Kellen physically hands the complete evidentiary package to the records custodian under a public-interest release procedure.
The custodian verifies the provenance seals and contributors while Axiom confirms that its unauthorized retention entry is included.
Journalists and oversight investigators wait on the public side of the archive as the custodian releases certified copies and access.
Questions immediately begin about government, research, insurance, security and commercial participation.
Kellen refuses any attempt to remove her own entries or Axiom's. Performance and story direction: Exposure happens through accountable custody, witnesses and consequences, not a publication screen.

dialogueInline.text: Complete provenance?
Complete.
My entries?
Included.
Yours?
Included.

dialogueInline.speaker: ARCHIVE CUSTODIAN
dialogueInline.text: Once released, all of it is public record.
Then leave it alone.

summary: Public reaction is explosive but not uniform. Some demand abolition of the regulatory system; others demand stronger safeguards against manipulation; many want current protections preserved while their origins are investigated. The Stack cannot simply return to the world before Issue 1.
panelPlan: Public reaction fills civic plazas, community halls and ordinary workplaces at once; the Stack continues functioning while people argue about what the disclosure means.
An Organic resident demands abolition of the registry while another argues to keep protections until exploit attacks stop.
Augment organizers split over integrity checks versus movement control; Baseline families who experienced attacks demand continuing safeguards.
John, Ostra, Nico and Kellen move through the disagreement rather than standing above it.

Government officials announce an emergency constitutional review in person or through ordinary press briefing while essential services remain running. Performance and story direction: The truth creates more politics, not a unified protest montage dependent on placards.

That doesn't mean anyone agrees what to do.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: Abolish the registry.

dialogueInline.speaker: BASELINE PARENT
dialogueInline.text: My son was attacked with that data. Don't remove the protection.

dialogueInline.speaker: AUGMENT ORGANIZER
dialogueInline.text: Keep integrity checks. End movement control.
Nobody even agrees what victory means.
Good. At least they're arguing about what actually exists now.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Classification authority is going under emergency constitutional review. Essential protections remain in force during review.

settingText: STACK-WIDE PUBLIC REACTION — mass demonstrations and ordinary civic life continue at once, with Organic, Augment and Baseline constituencies visibly disagreeing within their own groups. The government review announcement remains institutional rather than militarized.

summary: Issue end. A proposal to suspend Intelligence interpretation reaches the emergency coordination room. Instead of abstractly modeling collapse, staff walk through live cases already dependent on reconciliation and discover that transit, medicine, water, employment and security would begin failing within minutes.
panelPlan: A senior official proposes suspending automated interpretive authority until direct human control can be restored.
Rather than opening a systems model, Axiom asks each live operations desk what currently waits on reconciliation.
Transit has incompatible access orders, a clinic has a treatment/employment conflict, water has a route-and-hazard exception, and security is depending on the same shared priority logic.
Staff estimate when each real case becomes physical harm if nobody can resolve the cross-system conflicts; the first deadlines are inside forty minutes.

Final wide image: the living Stack outside the coordination room, with ordinary trains, hospitals and utilities all depending on the same administrative joints. Ostra concludes they cannot simply shut it down. Performance and story direction: Define Issue 8's problem through real people waiting on decisions.

dialogueInline.text: Suspend automated interpretation until direct human control is restored.
Transit desk. What is currently waiting on reconciliation?

dialogueInline.speaker: TRANSIT DISPATCHER
dialogueInline.text: Two access orders that can't both hold.
Medical?

dialogueInline.speaker: MEDICAL OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Treatment clears. Employment rule blocks the patient from getting there.
Water?

dialogueInline.speaker: UTILITY OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Hazard route conflict. We have maybe thirty-five minutes.
How long before this becomes physical?
Material failures begin inside forty minutes.
Because everything is tied through reconciliation now.
Then shutting it down isn't the answer.
No. We change who gets to make the calls.
